newsitem.title: THAILAND: Two Thai textile plants stop work due to high bills.
newsitem.headline: Two Thai textile plants stop work due to high bills.

text.p: Two big Thai textile manufacturing plants were forced to stop production after their owner was unable to pay electricity bills of 202 million baht ($7.77 million), officials and workers said on Wednesday.

Bophit Roikrong, head of the state-run Provincial Electricity Authority's (PEA) Rangsit unit, said negotiations were continuing with the owner of Thai American Textile Co Ltd and the Thai Melon Textile Co Ltd to settle the four-month-old electricity bills.
Both plants, which produce clothing, are owned by Chutipat Photiratnanangkul. He was not immediately available for comment.
Bophit told Reuters that the utility had never previously had problems with payments from either of the companies, which have been operating for about three decades.

Workers at Thai American Textile said the PEA had cut electricity lines at the two plants, located in Bangkok's neighbouring province of Pathum Thani, on May 1 after talks with the PEA broke down in April.
The two factories employ about 12,000 workers, about half of whom live in houses within the plants' compound.
Chutipat also holds majority shares in Thai Iryo Plc and Thai Melon Polyester Plc.
Thai Iryo has been suspended from trading on the Thai bourse since December 9 due to the company's poor performance.
Thai Melon Polyester was trading at 2.10 baht by 0515 GMT on Wednesday, down 0.20 baht from Tuesday.
